name: Least Count of Screw Gauge
variables: LC: Least count; Pitch: Distance moved in one complete rotation; Divisions: Circular scale graduations
meaning: Defines the smallest measurable thickness or diameter using micrometer screw gauge.
conditions: Applicable for standard pitch and circular scale screw gauges without uncorrected zero error.
example: If pitch is 0.5 mm and divisions = 50, then LC = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm.
commonMistake: Neglecting zero error: Correct reading = Observed Reading - (± Zero Error).

name: Horizontal Range of Projectile
formula: R = (u² sin 2θ) / g = (2 u_x u_y) / g
variables: u: Initial projection speed; θ: Angle of projection with horizontal; g: Acceleration due to gravity
meaning: Horizontal displacement of projectile from launch to return to same horizontal level.
conditions: Air resistance neglected; flat ground level.
example: At θ = 45°, Range is maximum: R_max = u² / g.
commonMistake: Thinking ranges are different for complementary angles: Angles θ and (90° - θ) have the EXACT same range.

name: Banking of Roads (Maximum Safe Speed)
formula: v_max = √[ r g (tan θ + μ) / (1 - μ tan θ) ]
variables: r: Radius of curvature; g: 9.8 m/s²; θ: Banking angle; μ: Coefficient of static friction
meaning: Maximum safe speed to negotiate a curved banked road without skidding outward.
conditions: When friction μ is zero, optimum speed v_opt = √(rg tan θ).
example: On frictionless ice-covered banked road: tan θ = v² / (rg).
commonMistake: Inverting numerator and denominator terms in the tangent-friction formula.

name: Escape Velocity from Planetary Surface
variables: G: Universal gravitational constant; M: Mass of planet; R: Radius of planet; g: Surface gravity
meaning: Minimum speed required for a projectile to permanently escape the gravitational pull of a celestial body.
conditions: Independent of mass of the projected body and angle of projection.
example: If mass of Earth quadruples and radius doubles: v_e' = √[2G(4M)/(2R)] = √2 · v_e.
commonMistake: Thinking escape velocity depends on the launch angle. It depends ONLY on the planet's mass and radius.

name: Carnot Engine Thermal Efficiency
variables: T_C: Temperature of cold reservoir (sink) in Kelvin; T_H: Temperature of hot reservoir (source) in Kelvin
meaning: Theoretical maximum efficiency of any heat engine operating between two thermal baths.
conditions: Temperatures MUST strictly be expressed in Kelvin (K), not Celsius.
example: For source at 400 K and sink at 300 K, η = 1 - 300/400 = 0.25 (25%).
commonMistake: Plugging temperatures in Celsius (°C), which yields wildly wrong answers.

name: YDSE Fringe Width
variables: λ: Wavelength of monochromatic light; D: Distance between slits and screen; d: Distance between the two coherent slits
meaning: Distance between any two consecutive bright or two consecutive dark interference fringes.
conditions: d << D and λ << d; Monochromatic coherent sources.
example: Immersing apparatus in water (μ = 4/3) reduces fringe width to β' = β / μ = 0.75 β.
commonMistake: Confusing slit width d with distance to screen D.
